online_exposures: social media use (any measure: frequency, daily duration, passive/active use, platform-specific use, number of platforms, or problematic/addictive use on a validated scale)
problematic or addictive social media use (BSMAS, SNAS, SMARS, PSMU): every pooled exposure measure in Tables 5a and 5b is one of these scales
population_notes: Adolescents and young adults from community, school or university samples (children under 10 and clinical inpatient psychiatric samples excluded). Pooled studies from USA, China, Hong Kong, Turkey, Lithuania, Germany; sample sizes 300 to 1,640; mean ages 15.60 to 21.47. No Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America or South/Southeast Asia.
last_search_date: April 2021 (end of publication-date window, 2010/01/01 to 2021/04/30; date the searches were run not reported)
primary_designs: 12 cross-sectional (all pooled studies); no longitudinal study or RCT contributed

narrative_summary: Pooled cross-sectional evidence from 12 studies: social media use (in practice problematic-use scales) correlated positively with depressive (k = 10) and anxiety (k = 7) symptoms; the two associations did not differ across 5 shared samples; the depression association was weaker in samples with mean age below 19; the anxiety prediction interval included zero.
narrative_locator: Discussion, Principal Findings. Quote: "This meta-analysis found positive associations between social media use and both depressive and anxiety symptoms among adolescents and young adults."
author_conclusion: Social media use is positively associated with depressive and anxiety symptoms at small-to-moderate magnitude with no difference between outcomes; the anxiety prediction interval includes zero, the depression association is weaker in adolescent samples, and cross-sectional data preclude causal inference.
rob_tool_used: Newcastle-Ottawa Scale adapted for cross-sectional designs (NOS-CS, 10 points) and NOS cohort version (9 points), two reviewers; no study-level or summary scores reported (Supplementary Table S2 is cited but is not in the supplementary file)

critical_flaws: 4: search limited to English-language, peer-reviewed articles published January 2010 to April 2021 (preprints excluded) with no justification for any restriction; the window ends more than five years before publication; per-database yields never reported (Results placeholder, supplement note saying yields still to be completed); no expert contact

9: NOS named in Methods, but no study-level or summary risk-of-bias results are reported anywhere; Supplementary Table S2 is absent from the supplementary file and Table 3 says NOS scores are still to be finalised
noncritical_weaknesses: 6: N, one reviewer extracted with verification by a second (not duplicate extraction), and two pooled entries are labelled '[source unverified]' in Tables 5a and 5b
8: PY, country, n, mean age, exposure and outcome instruments and design given per study, but recruitment setting and sex composition not reported per study
10: N, funding sources of included studies not reported

12: N, no assessment of how risk of bias affects the pooled estimates is reported (low-risk sensitivity analysis and NOS meta-regression are said to be in Supplementary Table S2, which is absent; Table 7 D5 says quality subgroups were not conducted)
amstar2.notes: Item 2 Y: PROSPERO CRD42024421214 stated as registered in advance and deviations justified in Table 7; whether registration preceded the search cannot be checked because the search execution date is not reported and the number appears to be a 2024 registration while the window ends April 2021. Item 3 Y on a lenient reading: observational design justified by the exposure question (Cochrane Handbook ch. 24); RCT inclusion not explained. Item 4 judgment call: the project rule's PY clause read literally (two or more databases plus strategy, missing expert contact) would give PY; rated N because AMSTAR 2 (Shea 2017) requires justified publication restrictions even for PY, and there is no evidence of executed yields. With item 4 at PY the overall would be Low. Item 7 Y: Table 4 itemizes the 3 full-text exclusions with reasons and the text says 15 studies reached full text, but the PRISMA flow counts are a placeholder, so completeness cannot be verified. Item 9 judgment call: if credited as PY (NOS covers selection and comparability), the overall would be Low (one critical flaw). Item 13 Y: Discussion addresses shared-method variance from self-report, convenience university samples and cross-sectional design as likely inflating or confounding associations. Item 15 Y: Egger and trim-and-fill reported and discussed as underpowered; contour-enhanced funnel plots are cited as supplementary figures but are not in the supplementary file.

extraction_notes: TABLE RECONSTRUCTION (two-column extraction printed cells out of order): Table 5a rows rebuilt by matching r values to the CI sequence: Holmgren & Coyne 0.290; Wang 0.180; Hou 0.220 (its outcome 'DASS-21 (Dep)' printed after the next row); Kircaburun & Griffiths [33] 0.030; Kircaburun, Demetrovics 0.220; Kircaburun & Griffiths (2020) 0.340; Stockdale & Coyne 0.280; Wong 0.336; Brailovskaia LT 0.305; Brailovskaia DE 0.396; pooled 0.263. Table 5b: Hou 0.220; Stockdale 0.240; Wong 0.384; Yildiz Durak 0.580; Brailovskaia LT 0.246; Brailovskaia DE 0.411 (printed out of sequence); Kilincel & Muratdagi 0.417; pooled 0.363. Both reconstructions agree with the within-study Fisher z differences in the Comparison Between Outcomes section and with the min/max values in the text. Per-study weights in Table 5a could not be matched to rows with certainty (not extracted). Table 6 rows rebuilt from column order; all pooled values match the text and abstract. Table 4 rows rebuilt (rows 1-12 pooled, 3/7/8/9/10 in both analyses); exclusion reasons assigned to rows 13-15 (Apaolaza, He, Mitra & Rangaswamy) in printed order. Table 7 label D4 is printed apart from its row (outcome definition, stress subscales excluded). REPORTING PROBLEMS: Results contain an unfilled placeholder ('[Per-database yields and stage-by-stage counts to be inserted ...]') and no PRISMA counts; Methods say Supplementary Table S1 gives yields, but S1 contains a 'Note to author team' that yields must still be completed and unobserved yields must not be reported. Supplementary Table S2 (NOS scores, low-risk sensitivity analysis, NOS meta-regression), File S3 (analysis script) and funnel plots are cited but are not in the supplementary file. Table 3 says the RoB moderator is 'To be tested once study-level NOS scores are finalised', which contradicts the Results claims. Two pooled entries are labelled '[source unverified]' (Kircaburun & Griffiths (2020), which has no reference number, and Brailovskaia et al. LT, which feeds both analyses), contradicting the Strengths claim that every estimate was verified against source and failures excluded. Anxiety text refers to 'removal of the two entries described above' but no such entries are described. Data Extraction says non-pooled and adjusted-only studies were kept for narrative synthesis; Table 7 D7 says no narrative synthesis was done. The citation and record title ('A Global Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis') differs from the article heading ('A Meta-Analysis of Systematically Searched Evidence') even though D7 says the title now matches. He et al. was excluded partly for 'design mismatch (randomised trial)' although RCTs were eligible. Kappa values said to be computed are not reported. Identical mean ages printed for Wang and Kircaburun & Griffiths [33] (16.29) and for Yildiz Durak and Kilincel & Muratdagi (15.60), copied as printed. NUMBERS NOT RECORDED AS FINDINGS: prediction intervals: depression 0.031 to 0.468; anxiety −0.009 to 0.646; depression mean age <19 −0.370 to 0.656; anxiety <19 not reported (k = 3). Paired anxiety-minus-depression comparison over 5 shared samples: mean Fisher z difference −0.007, t(4) = −0.32, p = .77, Wilcoxon p = .88; unpaired z = 1.71, p = .088. Striking meta-regression: mean sample age predicted the depression association (b = 0.045 per year, SE = 0.020, z = 2.27, p = .023), residual Q(8) = 4.24, p = .84; no age gradient for anxiety. Leave-one-out: depression 0.247 to 0.289; anxiety 0.322 to 0.385; anxiety without Wong r = 0.359 (95% CI 0.249 to 0.461; k = 6; N = 4,986; I² = 94.4%). OTHER: n_participants_total left null because no combined unique total is reported (depression N = 5,774 and anxiety N = 5,286 share five samples). All pooled estimates are crude, and every exposure instrument is a problematic/addictive-use scale, so estimates speak to problematic use more than general use (authors agree). population_age set to 'adolescents' following the title and registered population; the pool spans late adolescence and emerging adulthood (6 of 10 depression samples have mean age 19 or above). Outcomes outside the condition list: psychological distress (protocol secondary outcome, not reported) and stress subscales (excluded). The review discloses AI use for language editing only.
